newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Officials must answer for their actions - Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Officials must answer for their actions - Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who is recovering from open heart surgery, warned officials on Tuesday to be ready to answer for actions they undertook during his absence, a Kremlin spokesman said.

"After (Yeltsin's) return to the Kremlin representatives of the executive branch of power at all levels will have to answer for decisions they made, for their consequences and for their mistakes," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had issued his warning during a meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, his first full working meeting since his quintuple bypass operation on November 5. He did not elaborate.
He said Yeltsin had worked for four hours on Sunday and that the president expected to leave the Central Clinical Hospital for the Barvikha sanatorium some time this week.

Yeltsin's nearly four-month absence from the Kremlin, caused by heart problems that ended in the operation, has been marked by a worsening economic crisis and an upsurge in the behind-the-scenes power struggle among the president's entourage.
Yeltsin's aides have also expressed concerns about the way influential regional leaders are increasingly ignoring Moscow.
Yeltsin's chief of staff Anatoly Chubais has said one of the first things on Yeltsin's agenda once doctors allow him to return to work would be to summon regional bosses to call them to order.
